title: The city that stopped printing parking tickets
dek: Eighteen months after Harrow turned off its enforcement cameras, the budget did not collapse. Here is what did change.

blocks.alt: Geometric plate: a folded city map
blocks.caption: Harrow's downtown, redrawn.

blocks.text: When Harrow turned off its enforcement cameras, the finance office predicted a two-million-dollar hole. The hole arrived. The collapse did not.
Ticket revenue had been 4 percent of the general fund. The city covered the gap with a small parking-meter increase and a hiring freeze that was already planned.

blocks.title: Downtown trips by mode, after the change
blocks.alt: Bars compare the change in trips by car, bus, bike, and on foot.
blocks.caption: Source: Harrow transport office, fictional demo data.

blocks.quote: We expected a hole. We got a different city.
blocks.attribution: Harrow city treasurer, in this demo
